proposed_widenings.name: passive_grant (ClassFeatureMechanics family)
proposed_widenings.justification: Subclass selection is a permanent, one-time character-build decision with no activation cost, no resource, and no reset cadence. The current ClassFeatureMechanics union has only 'activation', which requires all three. A 'passive_grant' family (or 'permanent_unlock') is needed for features that are simply acquired and never activated.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Barbarian level or lower.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_subclass_access
proposed_widenings.justification: The effect of this feature is granting access to a subclass feature tree. The v4 taxonomy has 'grant_spell_access' for spells but no equivalent for subclass features. 'grant_subclass_access' would carry the subclass identity and the rule that features are acquired at or below the current class level.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice... A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels.

notes: No honest encoding is possible under the current surface. The 'activation' family is the only ClassFeatureMechanics family and it requires activationCost + UseCountResource + resetCadence + one of two specific effects (grant_extra_action, heal_hp). This feature has none of those — it is a passive, permanent subclass unlock. A new 'passive_grant' mechanics family and a 'grant_subclass_access' effect atom are the minimum additions needed. The same structural gap applies to all other 'Subclass' features across classes (bard L3, cleric L3, druid L3, fighter L3, monk L3, paladin L3, ranger L3, rogue L3, sorcerer L3, warlock L3, wizard L3).
